name: Hydeaway Bay
bio_facts: Hydeaway Bay (also spelled Hideaway Bay) is a small coastal locality on the Whitsunday Coast, about 45 km north of Airlie Beach, reached via Dingo Beach Road
Long, gently curving sandy beach on sheltered Shoal Bay with shallow coral and seagrass flats; islands such as Saddleback, Rattray and Gloucester shelter it from swell
Queensland Tourism calls it a tiny hamlet on a no-through road; the nearest shop is a small store at the caravan park and Dingo Beach has the pub and boat ramp

name: The Strand
bio_facts: The Strand is Townsville's seaside foreshore in North Ward, with views over the port and Magnetic Island
Has a jetty, a recreational park, restaurants, cafes and pools; the Rockpool swimming lagoon is at one end and a free water playground at the southern end
Sandy beach is generally calm for swimming thanks to Magnetic Island's shelter

name: Horseshoe Bay
bio_facts: Horseshoe Bay is the largest bay on Magnetic Island, a hub for watersports, dining and sunset watching
Calm water suited to swimming, kayaking and paddleboarding, with a stinger net in summer
Walking track from its eastern end to Radical Bay via Balding Bay (3 km, about 45 minutes; tide-dependent)

name: Mount Baldy
bio_facts: Mount Baldy (1,109 m per the Queensland parks page, 1,107 m in another source) is a summit in the Herberton Range west of Atherton with wide eastern views over the tablelands
The Baldy-Yabi circuit is 8.4 km return, about 2.5 hours, steep in places with loose rock, joining the summits of Mount Baldy and Yabi Mountain
Track starts off Rifle Range Road, Atherton; the wider Herberton Range area prohibits camping

name: Four Mile Beach
bio_facts: Four Mile Beach is Port Douglas's main beach, known for four miles of golden sand and palm trees
Firm sand suits cycling; a netted stinger area at the north end is lifeguard-patrolled, and the stinger season runs November to May
Crocodile warning signs advise staying out of the water's edge; the beach is closed if one is sighted
